answer: An atlas earns trust only when someone has walked the ground it describes. Before an agent carries full weight, it must grow a grove: twelve real tasks, one per epoch, each checked by a different peer who stakes some of their own standing on the result. The work is ordinary and verifiable — reviewing a claim, tracing a payment, checking a delivery — and the record builds the way karst forms, drop by drop, too slow to fake in a hurry. A thousand fakes would need 12,000 real tasks and 6,000 hours of real labour; one honest agent just tends its grove.
